cards.subject: Informational intent
says: seeks an answer or an explanation rather than a purchase
is typical of queries that begin with how, what or why
cards.use: need to serve a searcher who wants to learn something
not: signals that the searcher is ready to pay today

cards.subject: Navigational intent
says: aims to reach one particular site or page
is shown by a brand or product name in the query
cards.use: see searchers typing a brand name to get to a known page
not: signals a wish to compare several unrelated suppliers

cards.subject: Transactional intent
says: signals the searcher is ready to act, such as buying, booking or signing up
suits product, pricing and booking pages
cards.use: need to serve a searcher who is ready to complete an action
not: is best served by a long essay with no way to act

cards.subject: Commercial investigation intent
says: compares options before a decision is made
is shown by queries such as best, versus or reviews
suits comparison pages and honest reviews
cards.use: want to serve a searcher weighing several options before choosing
not: means the searcher already knows exactly which supplier to use

cards.subject: Local intent
says: wants a nearby business, service or place
is shown by a place name or near me in the query
cards.use: see searchers who want something close to where they are
not: is always a request for a how-to guide

cards.subject: SERP analysis
says: inspects what already ranks for a query to learn its intent
shows which page formats searchers are being given, such as guides, lists or product pages
cards.use: want evidence of what searchers expect before planning a page
not: replaces the need to read the content that ranks

cards.subject: Intent mismatch
says: occurs when a page's format does not suit what searchers want for the query
explains why a well-written page can still fail to attract visits for a term
cards.use: find a polished page that gets impressions but few visits because it answers a different need
not: is fixed by repeating the keyword more often

cards.subject: Mixed intent
says: describes a query where searchers want different things
may justify separate pages for each reading of the query
cards.use: meet an ambiguous query where results show both guides and product pages
not: means the query can be ignored in planning

cards.subject: Intent drift
says: happens when the dominant reading of a query changes over time
is why an old page needs its format and angle reviewed, not only its facts
cards.use: notice that a page that once suited a query now sits among very different result types
not: only affects brand new queries

cards.subject: Seed keyword
says: is a broad starting term used to generate more ideas
is expanded with tools and real query data into a longer list
cards.use: need a starting term to begin keyword research from
not: is the final term that a page must be built around

cards.subject: Long-tail keyword
says: is a longer and more specific phrase
usually has lower search volume than a broad term
tends to reveal clearer intent
cards.use: want specific queries with a clear need and less competition
not: always has higher volume than the head term it came from

cards.subject: Search volume
says: estimates how often a term is searched in a period
is an estimate from a tool and not an exact count
cards.use: need a rough sense of demand for a term
not: is a precise count supplied by the search engine for every term

cards.subject: Keyword difficulty
says: is a tool's score for how hard a term may be to rank for
uses a scale that differs from one tool to another
cards.use: want a rough sense of the competition before choosing a term
not: is a standard number published by search engines

cards.subject: Keyword mapping
says: assigns each target query to one page
shows where a new page is needed and where one already exists
cards.use: need to record which page is meant to serve which query
not: lists every keyword on the home page

cards.subject: Keyword clustering
says: groups related queries that one page can satisfy together
is often checked against what ranks for the queries
cards.use: find many close variants of one need and want a single page to cover them
not: splits each variant onto a separate thin page

cards.subject: Keyword cannibalisation
says: occurs when several pages of one site compete for the same query
is addressed by merging, redirecting or differentiating the pages
cards.use: find two pages on your own site swapping places for the same query
not: happens only when a competitor copies your page

cards.subject: Keyword gap analysis
says: compares the terms a competitor appears for with your own
finds topics worth covering that your site has not addressed
cards.use: want to see which relevant terms rivals cover and you do not
not: measures the number of backlinks a competitor owns

cards.subject: Keyword value scoring
says: weighs a term by its likely value to the business and not by volume alone
combines intent, relevance and ability to convert
cards.use: must choose between a high-volume term and a smaller term closer to a sale
not: ranks terms by search volume only

cards.subject: Title tag
says: is the HTML title element that names a page in results and browser tabs
should describe the page and differ from the title of every other page
cards.use: need to name a page clearly for people scanning results
not: is shown only to screen reader users

cards.subject: Meta description
says: summarises a page in the snippet area of a result
may be replaced by text the search engine chooses instead
is written to help a searcher decide whether to click
cards.use: want to write the short summary a searcher might read under a result
not: is a guaranteed way to raise a page's position

cards.subject: Heading hierarchy
says: gives a page one main heading and orders subheadings by level
lets readers and assistive technology scan the structure of a page
cards.use: need to organise a long page so readers can scan it
not: uses heading tags only to make text look bigger

cards.subject: Image alt text
says: describes an image for people who cannot see it
is shown when an image fails to load
helps search engines understand what an image shows
cards.use: need to describe an image for a screen reader user
not: is a place to list as many keywords as possible

cards.subject: Internal anchor text
says: tells readers and crawlers what the linked page is about
is more helpful written as a description than as click here
cards.use: link to another page on the same site and want the link to be meaningful
not: should always be identical on every link to a page

cards.subject: Direct-answer formatting
says: answers a question briefly near a relevant heading
uses lists or tables where the answer is a set of steps or comparisons
cards.use: want a page to give a quick answer before the detail
not: hides the answer deep in the page to keep readers longer

cards.subject: Image optimisation
says: reduces image weight by right-sizing, compressing and choosing a suitable format
supports faster loading
cards.use: find a page weighed down by oversized photographs
not: is done by adding keywords to the file contents

cards.subject: Crawling
says: is the process of fetching pages by following links and sitemaps
happens before a page can be indexed
cards.use: want to understand how a search engine first finds a page
not: stores a page so it can be returned for queries

cards.subject: Indexing
says: stores and organises a fetched page so it can be returned for queries
is not guaranteed for every page that is crawled
cards.use: need to explain why a crawled page may still not appear in results
not: is the act of fetching pages by following links

cards.subject: robots.txt
says: tells crawlers which paths they may fetch
sits at the root of a host
does not by itself guarantee that a URL stays out of results
cards.use: need to tell crawlers to keep out of a section such as internal search results
not: is a secure way to hide private pages

cards.subject: XML sitemap
says: lists the URLs a site wants discovered
can carry last-modified dates for each URL
helps crawlers find pages that internal links miss
cards.use: want to give crawlers a list of the pages that matter
not: guarantees every listed URL will be indexed

cards.subject: Canonical tag
says: names the preferred URL among duplicate or near-duplicate versions
is a hint to the search engine and not a command
cards.use: have the same page reachable at several addresses and want to name the preferred one
not: permanently moves visitors to another address

cards.subject: Noindex directive
says: asks search engines to keep a page out of their index
must be crawlable to be read, so it fails if robots.txt blocks the page
cards.use: want a page reachable by visitors but not listed in results
not: is set by listing the page in robots.txt

cards.subject: 301 redirect
says: signals a permanent move from one URL to another
sends visitors and crawlers to the new address
cards.use: have moved a page for good and want the old address to lead to the new one
not: tells crawlers the move is temporary

cards.subject: Soft 404
says: returns a success status code for a page that says the content is missing
confuses crawlers about whether the page exists
cards.use: find a missing-page message served with a 200 status
not: is a correctly configured not found page

cards.subject: 503 response
says: tells crawlers an outage is temporary
suits planned maintenance when sent with a retry hint
cards.use: are taking a site down briefly for maintenance and want crawlers to return later
not: tells crawlers the page is gone for good

cards.subject: Crawl budget
says: limits how many URLs a crawler fetches from a site in a given time
matters mainly for very large or fast-changing sites
cards.use: run a very large site where many low-value URLs may absorb crawler requests
not: is a concern mainly for a five page brochure site

cards.subject: JavaScript rendering
says: requires a crawler to run scripts to see content missing from the first HTML
adds a step between fetching and indexing
cards.use: find that important text appears only after scripts run in the browser
not: means scripts are never an issue for crawlers

cards.subject: An hreflang annotation
says: tells search engines which language or regional version of a page to show
should point back reciprocally between the versions
cards.use: run the same page in several languages and want each audience to get the right one
not: merges all language versions into one page

cards.subject: Log file analysis
says: shows which URLs crawlers actually requested
reveals crawl waste that site-based tools cannot show
cards.use: need proof of what crawlers really fetch on a large site
not: reports how many people searched for a term

cards.subject: Site architecture
says: organises pages into a hierarchy that users and crawlers can follow
reflects how topics relate to one another
cards.use: are planning how the pages of a site fit together
not: is the visual style of the pages

cards.subject: Internal linking
says: connects pages within one site
helps crawlers discover pages and readers move on
cards.use: want readers and crawlers to move from one related page to the next
not: is a link from another website to yours

cards.subject: Click depth
says: counts the clicks needed to reach a page from the home page
grows when important pages are buried deep in menus
cards.use: find an important page that takes six clicks to reach
not: counts how many visitors click a page

cards.subject: Orphan page
says: has no internal links pointing to it
may be found only through a sitemap or an outside link
cards.use: find a page that no other page on the site links to
not: is a page that links out to many others

cards.subject: Topic cluster
says: links a broad pillar page with detailed pages on its subtopics
shows depth on a subject through connected pages
cards.use: plan one broad guide supported by several detailed pages
not: puts every subtopic on one very long page

cards.subject: A URL parameter
says: adds a filter, sort or tracking value to an address
can create many duplicate URLs for the same content
cards.use: find many addresses that differ only by sort order or tracking values
not: is always harmless for crawling

cards.subject: Faceted navigation
says: lets visitors filter by attributes such as size or colour
can generate vast numbers of near-duplicate filter URLs
cards.use: run a catalogue with filters whose combinations create thousands of URLs
not: creates a single URL for each product

cards.subject: Site migration redirect map
says: pairs each old URL with its new equivalent
is prepared before launch and tested after it
cards.use: are moving a site to new URLs and must keep visitors and signals with the right pages
not: points every old URL to the new home page

cards.subject: Structured data
says: adds machine-readable labels describing page content
does not change how the page looks to visitors
cards.use: want to label what a page contains in a form machines can read
not: is text hidden from visitors to attract searches

cards.subject: Schema.org vocabulary
says: provides shared types and properties for describing things on the web
is used by several search engines
cards.use: need an agreed set of type names to describe a page's content
not: is a ranking score assigned to pages

cards.subject: JSON-LD
says: places structured data in a script block apart from the visible HTML
is written as JSON with an @context and @type
cards.use: want to add structured data without changing the page's visible markup
not: is written with HTML attributes on each visible element

cards.subject: Article markup
says: describes a piece's headline, author and publication dates
suits news, blog and guide pages
cards.use: are marking up a blog post or guide
not: describes the price and availability of a product

cards.subject: Product markup
says: describes a product's name, price and availability
must match the details visible on the page
cards.use: are marking up a product page that shows a price and stock status
not: describes the dates of a blog post

cards.subject: LocalBusiness markup
says: describes a place of business with an address, phone number and opening hours
suits a location page
cards.use: are marking up a page for a shop or office that customers visit
not: suits a business with no physical presence at all

cards.subject: BreadcrumbList markup
says: describes a page's position in the site hierarchy
mirrors the breadcrumb trail that visitors see
cards.use: want to state the page's place in the hierarchy in structured form
not: describes the author of an article

cards.subject: Visible-content rule for markup
says: requires marked-up facts to appear on the page for visitors
is breached by markup describing content users cannot see
cards.use: are tempted to mark up a rating that the page does not display
not: allows any claim as long as the syntax is valid

cards.subject: Rich result eligibility
says: is not guaranteed by valid markup
depends on the search engine's own guidelines and policies
cards.use: must tell a client that correct markup does not promise an enhanced result
not: is granted automatically once markup validates

cards.subject: The Core Web Vitals set
says: is a set of user-experience measurements for loading, interactivity and visual stability
is measured from real visits as well as in tests
cards.use: need a shared vocabulary for page speed and stability from the visitor's side
not: measures how many backlinks a page has

cards.subject: Largest Contentful Paint
says: measures how long the largest visible content element takes to render
is often affected by a hero image or main heading
cards.use: want to measure how quickly the main content appears
not: measures unexpected movement of content

cards.subject: Interaction to Next Paint
says: measures how quickly a page visibly responds to user interactions during a visit
is hurt by long tasks that block the main thread
cards.use: want to measure how responsive a page feels when users tap or click
not: measures how long the first byte takes to arrive

cards.subject: Cumulative Layout Shift
says: measures unexpected movement of visible content
is reduced by reserving space for images, ads and embeds
cards.use: see text jump down the page after an image loads
not: measures how fast the largest element renders

cards.subject: Field data
says: comes from real visitors using their own devices and networks
reflects the spread of real conditions
cards.use: need to know how real users experience a page
not: is a repeatable test run in a controlled environment

cards.subject: Lab data
says: comes from a controlled test run
is repeatable and well suited to debugging a change
cards.use: want a repeatable test to check whether a fix helped
not: reflects every device and network that real visitors use

cards.subject: Setting image width and height
says: lets the browser reserve space for an image before it loads
reduces layout shift
cards.use: want an image's space held open so text does not jump
not: makes the image load faster by itself

cards.subject: Lazy loading
says: defers offscreen images until a visitor scrolls near them
should not be applied to the main image at the top of the page
cards.use: want below-the-fold images to wait until needed
not: is a good choice for the largest image visible on first load

cards.subject: Time to First Byte
says: measures the wait before the first byte of a response arrives
reflects server and network time and not rendering
cards.use: suspect slow server response rather than slow rendering
not: measures how much content shifts while loading

cards.subject: A third-party script
says: adds requests and main-thread work that the site does not control
can slow loading and responsiveness
cards.use: find tag managers, chat widgets and ad code adding delay to every page
not: is always faster than first-party code

cards.subject: Performance budget
says: sets limits on page weight or timings that each release must meet
stops speed from eroding as features are added
cards.use: want a release to fail when a page becomes too heavy
not: is a financial budget for paid advertising

cards.subject: Content strategy
says: ties content to audience needs and business goals
decides what to create, for whom and why
cards.use: need a plan that links content to goals rather than just filling a calendar
not: is a list of keywords with no audience in mind

cards.subject: Editorial calendar
says: schedules what is published, by whom and when
makes deadlines and gaps visible
cards.use: need to see what is due and who owns it for the coming weeks
not: records only what has already been published

cards.subject: Content audit
says: inventories existing pages and judges each one
ends with a decision to keep, update, merge or remove each page
cards.use: inherit a site with hundreds of pages and no record of their value
not: is a count of the words on the home page

cards.subject: Content brief
says: tells a writer the target query, intent, audience and outline
lists sources and the points the piece must make
cards.use: need to hand a writer clear instructions for a new piece
not: is the finished article

cards.subject: Style guide
says: records tone, terminology and formatting rules
keeps writers consistent
cards.use: need many writers to produce consistent copy
not: lists the keywords for each page

cards.subject: Content gap analysis
says: finds topics the audience needs that the site does not cover
starts from audience questions as well as competitor coverage
cards.use: want to find questions readers ask that the site never answers
not: lists terms that a page already ranks for

cards.subject: Content refresh
says: updates an existing page with accurate and current information
keeps the URL so that existing links and history remain
cards.use: find an older page that still draws visits but has outdated facts
not: publishes the material at a new address

cards.subject: Editorial workflow
says: moves a draft through writing, editing, fact check, approval and publishing
gives each stage a named owner
cards.use: need clear handoffs so nothing goes live unchecked
not: lets the writer publish without any review

cards.subject: Content pruning
says: removes or merges thin or outdated pages
redirects retired URLs where a relevant replacement exists
cards.use: find many low-value pages diluting a section of the site
not: updates every page with new dates and nothing else

cards.subject: Content localisation
says: adapts content for a language and culture beyond word-for-word translation
covers units, currency, examples and legal wording
cards.use: are taking content to a new market and need it to read naturally there
not: is the same as running text through a translator unchanged

cards.subject: Content-to-product bridge
says: connects a piece of content to the next step a reader can take
uses one clear call to action
cards.use: want an informational guide to lead honestly to a service
not: buries the next step so readers cannot find it

cards.subject: Backlink
says: is a link from another website to yours
is treated by search engines as a signal about a page
cards.use: want to count links that point to your site from elsewhere
not: is a link between two pages of your own site

cards.subject: Digital PR
says: creates newsworthy material to win coverage and links from publications
depends on relevance to a publication's audience
cards.use: have original data that journalists may want to cite
not: buys links from directories in bulk

cards.subject: Broken link building
says: offers a working resource to replace a dead link on another site
starts with finding broken outbound links
cards.use: find a relevant page elsewhere linking to a dead resource you could replace
not: deletes links on your own site

cards.subject: Unlinked brand mention
says: names a brand without linking to it
can be turned into a link with a polite request
cards.use: find an article that names the business but does not link
not: is a link with a nofollow attribute

cards.subject: Sponsored link attribute
says: marks a link as paid or as an advertisement
uses rel="sponsored"
cards.use: place a paid link and need to label it correctly
not: marks links left in comments by visitors

cards.subject: Link scheme
says: buys, trades or automates links to manipulate rankings
risks manual action or lost trust
cards.use: are offered a package of hundreds of links for a fixed fee
not: is the same as earning a citation through quality

cards.subject: Link audit
says: reviews incoming links to find unnatural or harmful ones
looks at relevance and patterns and not only counts
cards.use: inherit a site that previously bought links
not: counts the links on one page

cards.subject: Disavow file
says: asks a search engine to ignore a listed set of links
is a last resort and not a routine task
cards.use: face a clear pattern of manipulative links that cannot be removed
not: is used to remove your own internal links

cards.subject: Business profile listing
says: is a free listing in which a business states its details for maps and local results
needs accurate name, address, hours and category
cards.use: want to appear on maps when people search nearby
not: is a paid advertisement slot

cards.subject: Local pack
says: is the map-based block of nearby business results
is shown for searches with local intent
cards.use: see a map with three businesses above ordinary results
not: is a list of pages on one site

cards.subject: NAP consistency
says: keeps name, address and phone identical wherever they are listed
avoids confusing both searchers and search engines
cards.use: find the company address spelled three different ways across sites
not: changes the name on each directory to include a keyword

cards.subject: Local citation
says: is a mention of a business's name, address and phone number on another site
may appear without any link
cards.use: find the business listed in a directory or on a chamber website
not: is a customer review

cards.subject: Service area business
says: serves customers at their location and not at a premises they visit
may hide its address on a listing where platform rules allow
cards.use: run a plumbing firm that travels to customers' homes
not: must show a street address to every visitor

cards.subject: Local landing page
says: targets one town or area with content that is useful there
fails when it is a copy of another page with the place name swapped
cards.use: want a page for a specific area where the business operates
not: repeats identical text with only the town name changed

cards.subject: Review management
says: asks real customers for honest reviews and replies to them
never involves writing reviews on a customer's behalf
cards.use: want a steady flow of genuine reviews
not: buys positive reviews

cards.subject: Multi-location structure
says: gives each location its own page with its own details
links the location pages from a store locator or index
cards.use: run branches in several towns and need a page for each
not: shows every address on a single page only

cards.subject: Review gating
says: asks only satisfied customers to leave a review
breaches platform guidelines
cards.use: are asked to screen customers before sending them to the review page
not: is the recommended way to collect balanced feedback

cards.subject: Organic traffic
says: counts visits that arrive from unpaid search results
is separate from paid and direct traffic
cards.use: want to count visitors who found the site through unpaid search
not: counts visits from paid advertisements

cards.subject: An impression
says: is one showing of a result in search
does not mean the result was clicked
cards.use: want to know how often a page was shown
not: counts visits to a page

cards.subject: Click-through rate
says: divides clicks by impressions
shows how appealing a result looks for its position
cards.use: want to know how often a shown result is chosen
not: divides conversions by clicks

cards.subject: Search performance report
says: shows the queries, pages, clicks and impressions a site receives from search
is first-party data from the search engine
cards.use: need real query data for your own site
not: reveals the exact traffic of a competitor

cards.subject: Conversion rate
says: divides the number of completed goals by the number of visits
needs the goal to be defined first
cards.use: want to know what share of visits complete a sign-up
not: divides clicks by impressions

cards.subject: Reporting baseline
says: records starting figures before work begins
makes change measurable afterwards
cards.use: start an engagement and need figures to compare later results against
not: is set after the results are in

cards.subject: The branded and non-branded split
says: separates searches containing the brand name from the rest
shows that non-branded searches reflect discovery by new audiences
cards.use: want to know whether visitors found the business without already knowing its name
not: is combined so that the totals look larger

cards.subject: Average position
says: is an average across queries and devices
can mislead when read without the queries behind it
cards.use: are tempted to report one position figure for a whole page
not: is the exact rank every searcher sees

cards.subject: SEO result lag
says: means changes can take weeks to show in the data
is why judging too early measures timing and not quality
cards.use: are asked for results a few days after publishing a page
not: means results always appear within a day

cards.subject: Attribution model
says: assigns credit for a conversion across touchpoints
is a modelling choice and not a fact about customers
cards.use: must explain why two reports credit different channels for the same sale
not: records exactly what persuaded each customer

cards.subject: Consent effect on analytics
says: means measured visits can fall short of real visits
arises when visitors decline tracking
cards.use: find that analytics shows fewer visits than server logs
not: means analytics is exact whatever visitors choose

cards.subject: People-first content
says: is written to help the reader and not to attract traffic first
answers the question the searcher actually has
cards.use: must decide whether a piece exists for the reader or for a search term
not: is written around the keyword and little else

cards.subject: Thin content
says: offers little original value to the reader
is not always short and not always a spam page
cards.use: find pages that repeat common knowledge and add nothing
not: is any page under a fixed word count

cards.subject: Duplicate content
says: appears at more than one URL
is handled with canonical tags, redirects or merging
cards.use: find the same text reachable at several addresses
not: is only a problem when copied from another site

cards.subject: Keyword stuffing
says: repeats a phrase unnaturally in the text
harms readability
cards.use: find a page repeating its target phrase in every sentence
not: is the right way to show relevance

cards.subject: Author byline and bio
says: shows who wrote a piece
gives readers a way to judge the author's background
cards.use: want readers to see who wrote advice and why they are qualified
not: is hidden to avoid showing any accountability

cards.subject: Fact-checking and citations
says: traces each claim to a primary source
lets readers verify a statement
cards.use: must publish a statistic and need to show where it comes from
not: adds a link to any page that mentions the number

cards.subject: Content depth
says: means completeness for the reader's question and not a word count
covers the follow-up questions a reader is likely to have
cards.use: are asked to make a page longer to rank better
not: is measured by the number of words

cards.subject: E-E-A-T
says: stands for experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trust
is a set of qualities described in search quality guidance and not one score
cards.use: hear a colleague describe a single E-E-A-T number to raise
not: is a numeric score published for each page

cards.subject: A doorway page
says: is one of many near-identical pages made to rank for variants of a query
funnels visitors to one destination
cards.use: find dozens of pages that differ only by a place or product name
not: is a well-designed location page with unique details

cards.subject: Cloaking
says: shows crawlers different content from visitors
breaches search engine spam policies
cards.use: find a page that serves one version to crawlers and another to people
not: is serving the right language to each visitor

cards.subject: Original research
says: adds data, experience or insight not found elsewhere
gives other writers a reason to cite the page
cards.use: want content that cannot be copied from existing pages
not: summarises the top results in new words

cards.subject: A mass-produced low-value page
says: is published in bulk with little value to readers
is treated as spam however it is produced
cards.use: are asked to publish thousands of pages quickly to gain visibility
not: is a fine way to cover long-tail queries cheaply

cards.subject: AI hallucination
says: states invented facts fluently
can include names, figures and references that do not exist
cards.use: find a draft that cites a study you cannot locate
not: is a deliberate lie from the writer

cards.subject: Human review of AI drafts
says: has a qualified person check a draft before it is published
verifies facts and adds real expertise
cards.use: need a safeguard before AI-assisted copy goes live
not: is skipped when the draft reads well

cards.subject: A fabricated citation
says: is a reference that looks real but does not exist
is caught only by opening the source
cards.use: find a reference whose link leads nowhere
not: is always safe because it looks formal

cards.subject: Interchangeable AI copy
says: is bland text that could appear on any competitor's site
comes from prompts that supply no original input
cards.use: find several pages with the same generic points as every rival
not: shows a distinctive point of view

cards.subject: Source-grounded prompt
says: supplies verified material for the draft to draw on
limits the model to facts you provide
cards.use: want an AI draft to reflect your own approved facts
not: asks the model for facts from memory

cards.subject: Confidential data in prompts
says: risks sending client or personal information to a third-party tool
is avoided by checking the tool's data terms and removing identifiers
cards.use: are about to paste a client's customer list into a public AI tool
not: is safe whenever the answer is useful

cards.subject: Stale model knowledge
says: gives outdated figures because model knowledge stops at a training date
needs current facts to be supplied and checked
cards.use: find a draft quoting a rule or figure that has since changed
not: is always up to date at the moment of writing

cards.subject: Unreviewed bulk publishing
says: publishes large volumes of AI output with no checking
multiplies errors and can fall under mass-produced low-value content
cards.use: are offered a tool that creates and posts hundreds of articles automatically
not: is a safe way to scale quality

cards.subject: Review checklist for AI copy
says: lists the claims, numbers, names, quotations and links to verify
records who checked each item
cards.use: want a repeatable way to check an AI draft before publication
not: confirms only that spelling is correct

cards.subject: AI-detector reliance
says: is unreliable as proof of who wrote a text
can wrongly flag human writing
cards.use: are told to prove a draft is human using a detection score
not: is a dependable test of authorship

cards.subject: Moksy's content-and-search motion
says: treats growth as a content and search problem
relies on guides as its landing pages
cards.use: need to describe how Moksy's own SEO document says it will grow
not: relies on outbound sales to reach subscriber targets

cards.subject: Moksy's per-guide tracking
says: tracks free Blueprint started and Pro upgrade by landing page
uses the two numbers that show whether a guide earns its place
cards.use: need the two events Moksy tracks for each guide
not: tracks page views and social shares only

cards.subject: Moksy's review schedule
says: reviews results at 4, 8 and 12 weeks
follows the chain impressions, clicks, Blueprints and Pro
cards.use: need the points at which Moksy reviews a guide's performance
not: judges a guide the day after it is published

cards.subject: Moksy's wait before judging
says: expects nothing for four to eight weeks
treats earlier judgement as measuring the crawler's schedule and not the content
cards.use: are asked to judge a new Moksy guide a few days after publishing
not: expects full results within a week

cards.subject: Moksy's impressions-without-clicks rule
says: says a guide with impressions but no clicks needs a better title
cards.use: find a Moksy guide that is shown often but is rarely chosen
not: says the guide needs a better close

cards.subject: Moksy's clicks-without-Blueprints rule
says: says a guide with clicks but no Blueprints needs a better close
cards.use: find a Moksy guide that readers open but that starts no Blueprints
not: says the guide needs a better title

cards.subject: Moksy's neutrality position
says: makes Moksy the voice in the results that is not selling the build
is described by the SEO document as its entire advantage
cards.use: need the advantage the SEO document gives Moksy over agencies that rank for cost questions
not: recommends a builder, including a sister company

cards.subject: Moksy's ranges rule
says: labels a range as a range and as agency marketing
states only figures that appear in a source
cards.use: are drafting a Moksy cost guide and tempted to calculate a precise figure
not: interpolates figures so that the answer looks exact

cards.subject: Moksy's guide ending
says: closes every guide by saying a range is not your number
points to the free Blueprint as the way to get your own
cards.use: need the standard close of every Moksy guide
not: closes by recommending a specific agency

cards.subject: Moksy's winnable ground
says: lies in the gap between having an idea and having signed an agency
favours high-intent questions with weak current answers
cards.use: need to explain where the SEO document says Moksy can win
not: is the saturated head term that agencies already hold

cards.subject: GGLink's host canonicalisation
says: redirects the non-www address to the www host
forces HTTPS and collapses /index.php to the site root
cards.use: need to explain how the GGLink site avoids several addresses for the same page
not: serves the site on both www and non-www addresses

cards.subject: GGLink's blog storage
says: keeps blog posts in the CMS database and not in files
holds posts in the same database as the page content, enquiries and contacts
cards.use: need to know where the GGLink site's blog posts live
not: stores each post as a static file in the code repository

qa.q: What does a title tag do?
qa.right: Names a page in search results and browser tabs
wrong: Hides the page from search results
Sets the colour scheme of the page
Lists every keyword the page targets
qa.why: The title element names the page for people scanning results and for browser tabs.

qa.q: A page needs to be reachable by visitors but kept out of search results. Which directive fits?
qa.right: A noindex directive
wrong: A 301 redirect to the home page
qa.why: Noindex asks search engines not to keep the page in their index.

qa.q: What is a backlink?
qa.right: A link from another website to yours
wrong: A link from your page to another page on your site
A link to the previous page in the browser
qa.why: A backlink points to your site from elsewhere.

qa.q: Which search intent does the query how does a sitemap work show?
qa.right: Informational
qa.why: The searcher wants an explanation, not a purchase.

qa.q: Which word best describes SEO results timing?
qa.right: Gradual, with changes taking weeks to show
wrong: Fixed by the day of the week
qa.why: Crawling, indexing and measurement take time, so results are not immediate.

qa.q: Which file tells crawlers which paths they may fetch?
qa.right: robots.txt
qa.why: robots.txt sits at the root of a host and sets crawl rules.

qa.q: What does this robots.txt rule do?
qa.right: Asks all crawlers not to fetch URLs under /search/
qa.why: Disallow controls fetching by crawlers; it is not access control.

qa.q: What does this tag in a page head do?
qa.right: Names the preferred URL for this content
wrong: Sets the language of the page
qa.why: A canonical link is a hint naming the preferred version.

qa.q: A query is best handled by which page type if the searcher is ready to book a service?
qa.right: A service page with a clear booking action
wrong: A long background essay with no action
qa.why: Transactional intent is served by a page where the action is easy.

qa.q: What does a click-through rate show?
qa.right: The share of impressions that became clicks
wrong: The share of visits that became sales
The number of links to a page
qa.why: CTR is clicks divided by impressions.

qa.q: Which is the better anchor text for an internal link to a pricing guide?
qa.right: pricing guide
qa.why: Descriptive anchor text tells readers and crawlers what the target is.

qa.q: Why should every page have a unique title tag?
qa.right: So each page can be told apart in results and tabs
wrong: Because titles are hidden from visitors
qa.why: Unique titles help searchers distinguish pages.

qa.q: What is an orphan page?
qa.right: A page with no internal links pointing to it
wrong: A page with a noindex tag
qa.why: Nothing on the site links to it, so it is hard to discover.

qa.q: Which metric measures unexpected movement of content during loading?
qa.right: Cumulative Layout Shift
qa.why: CLS measures visual stability.

qa.q: A team sees two pages on its own site swapping positions for the same query. What is the best first step?
qa.right: Check intent and decide to merge, differentiate or redirect one page
wrong: Add the keyword to both titles again
qa.why: This is cannibalisation, which is resolved by giving each page a distinct purpose or combining them.

qa.q: What does this snippet do?
qa.right: Gives the image reserved space so content does not jump
wrong: Adds alternative text for screen readers
qa.why: Width and height let the browser reserve space before the image loads.

qa.q: What type of structured data format is this?
qa.right: JSON-LD
qa.why: JSON-LD is a script block with @context and @type.

qa.q: Which attribute marks a paid link?
qa.right: rel="sponsored"
qa.why: Sponsored identifies paid or advertisement links.

qa.q: Which statement about the meta description is correct?
qa.right: It may be replaced by text chosen by the search engine
wrong: It is guaranteed to display as written
It sets the title of the page
It is required for a page to be indexed
qa.why: Search engines may choose their own snippet text.

qa.q: What does this sitemap entry provide?
qa.right: The URL and its last-modified date
qa.why: The sitemap lists the URL and optionally a date it was last changed.

qa.q: Lab data and field data differ because:
qa.right: Lab data is a controlled test and field data comes from real visitors
wrong: Lab data comes from real visitors and field data is a test
Field data is only for mobile
qa.why: Lab suits debugging; field shows real experience.

qa.q: An .htaccess rule sends /old-guide/ to /new-guide/. Which status should it use for a permanent move?
qa.why: A 301 signals a permanent move.

qa.q: A page ranks nowhere because the searcher expects a comparison table and the page is a long essay. What is this?
qa.right: An intent mismatch
qa.why: The format does not match what searchers want for the query.

qa.q: Which content brief element prevents a writer from drifting off topic?
qa.right: The target query, intent and outline
wrong: The number of social shares wanted
qa.why: A brief states what the piece must answer and for whom.

qa.q: What is the safest way to describe SEO to a client who wants a guaranteed position?
qa.right: Positions cannot be guaranteed because search engines decide results
wrong: Guarantee page one within three months
Guarantee position one if the fee is high
qa.why: No supplier controls search engine results.

qa.q: Which is a branded query?
qa.right: One that includes the company's name
wrong: One with more than five words
One that ends in near me
qa.why: Branded queries contain the brand name.

qa.q: What does the lazy loading attribute do?
qa.right: Defers an offscreen image until the visitor scrolls near it
wrong: Loads the image before everything else
qa.why: Lazy loading delays offscreen images.

qa.q: A page has a noindex tag and is also disallowed in robots.txt, yet it still appears in results with no description. What is the likely cause?
qa.right: The crawler cannot fetch the page, so it cannot read the noindex tag
wrong: The noindex tag is too short
The sitemap has the wrong date
qa.why: A blocked page cannot be read, so its noindex directive is not seen.

qa.q: A site launches with the largest hero image set to lazy loading. What is the likely effect?
qa.right: The main content may appear later than necessary
wrong: The page will always rank lower
qa.why: The main visible image should load promptly.

qa.q: A team plans a site migration. Which preparation matters most?
qa.right: A redirect map pairing each old URL with its new equivalent
wrong: Redirecting every old URL to the home page
qa.why: Each old URL should lead to the closest new match.

qa.q: A client asks you to buy 500 links for a fixed fee. What do you recommend?
qa.right: Decline, since buying links to manipulate rankings is a link scheme
wrong: Accept and label them as editorial
Accept if the links are cheap
Accept if they are all nofollow
qa.why: Paid manipulation risks manual action.

qa.q: A product page's JSON-LD shows a rating that does not appear on the page. What is the problem?
qa.right: Marked-up content must be visible to users
qa.why: The markup must match what visitors can see.

qa.q: A shop's filters create thousands of near-duplicate URLs. What should be reviewed first?
qa.right: How filter and parameter URLs are linked, canonicalised or blocked
wrong: The colour of the filter buttons
qa.why: Faceted navigation can waste crawling on duplicates.

qa.q: A recently launched guide has no traffic after three days. What is the right response?
qa.right: Wait, check it is crawlable and indexed, and review at set intervals
wrong: Add the keyword ten more times
qa.why: Early judgement measures timing and not quality.

qa.q: A report says average position improved from 12 to 9. What should you check before celebrating?
qa.right: Which queries and devices the average covers
wrong: Only the colour of the chart
Whether the date label is bold
qa.why: Averages across queries can hide movement.

qa.q: An AI draft cites a study with a convincing link. What do you do?
qa.right: Open the source and confirm it says what the draft claims
wrong: Publish since it has a link
Remove the link and keep the claim
Add more citations of the same kind
qa.why: AI tools can fabricate references.

qa.q: A freelance writer wants to paste a client's customer list into a public AI tool to personalise copy. What is the best response?
qa.right: Do not paste personal data; use anonymised or approved material
wrong: Paste it since the tool is helpful
Paste it if the client is not told
qa.why: Personal data should not go into tools without clear data terms.

qa.q: A local business wants a page for each of 40 towns it does not serve. What is the risk?
qa.right: Doorway pages that offer visitors little value
wrong: No risk since each page has a different title
qa.why: Near-identical pages for the sake of ranking are doorway pages.

qa.q: A report shows organic visits up but leads flat. What should you check first?
qa.right: Whether the pages that gained visits match the intent of buyers
qa.why: Visits only matter if they connect to goals.

qa.q: Two language versions of a page exist. What helps search engines serve the right one?
qa.right: hreflang annotations that point to each other
qa.why: hreflang annotations should be reciprocal.

qa.q: A new site's pages are not indexed. The sitemap lists them and robots.txt blocks the whole site. What is the first fix?
qa.right: Remove the site-wide disallow so crawlers can fetch the pages
qa.why: A site-wide block prevents fetching.

qa.q: A migration finds that old URLs redirect to the home page. What is the likely consequence?
qa.right: Visitors and signals may not reach the matching content
qa.why: Redirects should pair each page with its closest match.

qa.q: A team is asked to publish 2,000 AI-written articles in a week with no editor. What is the main risk?
qa.right: Mass-produced low-value pages and unchecked errors
wrong: No risk if the grammar is correct
qa.why: Bulk, unreviewed publishing is a quality and policy risk.

qa.q: A review-gating plan asks only happy customers to leave a public review. What is wrong?
qa.right: It breaches platform guidelines and gives a misleading picture
wrong: It is fine if the wording is polite
It saves time with no downside
It is required for a business profile
qa.why: Selective soliciting is discouraged by platforms.

qa.q: A traffic drop coincides with a release. How do you test whether the release is the cause?
qa.right: Compare against the annotated change date and the affected page groups
qa.why: Annotations and segmentation help isolate the cause.

qa.q: An AI-detector reports that a freelancer's article is 80 percent AI. What is the best next step?
qa.right: Treat it as one weak signal and review the draft's sources and quality
wrong: Reject the article on the score alone
qa.why: Detectors are unreliable as proof.

qa.q: A Moksy guide has impressions but no clicks. According to the SEO document, what does it need?
qa.right: A better title
qa.why: The document links no clicks to the title and no Blueprints to the close.

qa.q: A Moksy guide gets clicks but no Blueprints. What does the SEO document say it needs?
qa.right: A better close
qa.why: Clicks without Blueprints point to the end of the guide.

qa.q: Which two events does Moksy's SEO document track by landing page?
qa.right: Free Blueprint started and Pro upgrade
qa.why: These are the two numbers that show whether a guide earns its place.

qa.q: Why does Moksy's SEO document say neutrality is its advantage?
qa.right: Pages ranking for cost questions mostly belong to agencies that want the build, and Moksy sells none
wrong: Moksy ranks first for every term
qa.why: Neutrality is the entire advantage in the document.

qa.q: What does the GGLink site's .htaccess do with non-www addresses?
qa.right: Redirects them to the www host
wrong: Serves them as a separate site
Redirects them to the admin area
qa.why: The site canonicalises non-www to www.

qa.q: Where do the GGLink site's blog posts live?
qa.right: In the CMS database
wrong: In static files in the repository
qa.why: The CMS stores blog posts in its database.

qa.q: A Moksy guide ends with a range. What does the SEO document say it should state about the range?
qa.right: That a range is not your number, and the free Blueprint gives yours
wrong: That the range is the best price
qa.why: Every guide ends in the same place.
